newsitem.title: USA: Fed likely to refrain from open market operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed likely to refrain from open market operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve looks likely to refrain from open market operations on Tuesday, some analysts said.
Federal funds were trading at 5-7/16 percent in early dealings, below the Fed's 5-1/2 percent target for the rate.
"We look for the Fed to stay out," said Kim Rupert, senior economist at Standard & Poor's MMS.
However, Lee Youngdahl, bond market analyst at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co, said "a chance remains for a system repo.
"It looks like the (Fed) funds rate is comfortable, but I wouldn't rule out a system RP, even so," he said.
Rupert said the Fed could buy coupons as early as this week in a seasonal, but permanent, addition of reserves to the banking system.
But Youngdahl said that the more likely time for a permanent reserve addition would be next week and that the Fed was more likely to buy bills than coupons.

"Simply because the recent operations have been so heavily tilted toward (buying) coupons, they will probably decide to opt for bills to even things out a bit," said Youngdahl. "Also, bill auctions are larger these days than they have been in the past so that argues for bills."

The seasonal need for a permanent reserve addition intensifies as the three-day Labor Day holiday weekend approaches. This weekend traditionally marks the end of the summer vacation season and creates a jump in currency in circulation that drains reserves from the banking system.
"The daily add need will be in excess of $10.0 billion as we get toward the last week of August and the first week of September," said Youngdahl.
(( -- E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679))
